title: Coefficient and site squares for cartesian proper/open interchange
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings. Let
$k:U\hookrightarrow V$, $r:U\to W$, $p:V\to Z$, and $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$, with $pk=ir$,
be a cartesian square of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with $r,p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $k,i$ open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use ordinary constant-ring module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ on either site, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For a proper map $v$, let $q_v:T Rv_{*,A}\to Rv_{*,B}T$ be the $B$-linear adjoint transpose of $T$ of the $A$-counit, using the canonical pullback/tensor comparison. For an open immersion $a$, let $t_a:T a_{!,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}a_{!,B}T$ be the summandwise tensor comparison. Neither definition assumes $T$ preserves bounded-below complexes.

Let $\Gamma_R^{\rm et}:i_!Rr_{*,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{*,R}k_!$ be the specified proper/open map of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange]: it is the open adjunct of the inverse of open-restriction exchange followed by $k^*k_!=1$, with exchange the counit mate of the inverse-image square [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. For $E\in D^+(U_{\rm et},A)$ such that $E_B\in D^+(U_{\rm et},B)$, the following equality holds in the unbounded $B$-module derived category:
$$Rp_{*,B}(t_k(E))\circ q_p(k_{!,A}E)\circ T_Z(\Gamma_A^{\rm et}(E))
=\Gamma_B^{\rm et}(E_B)\circ i_{!,B}(q_r(E))\circ t_i(Rr_{*,A}E).$$

For each finite commutative ring $R$ let $N_T=\nu_T^*$ be exact site comparison, $e_a:N a_!^{\rm et}\xrightarrow{\sim}a_!^{\rm pro}N$ its canonical open-extension comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], and $d_v:N Rv_*^{\rm et}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv_*^{\rm pro}N$ its specified counit mate [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. On etale-origin bounded-below objects define $\Gamma_R^{\rm pro}$ by the same open-adjunction prescription using the site transports of the open-restriction exchange and the open unit. For every $E\in D^+(U_{\rm et},R)$, these specified maps satisfy
$$Rp_{*,R}^{\rm pro}(e_k(E))\circ d_p(k_!^{\rm et}E)\circ N_Z(\Gamma_R^{\rm et}(E))
=\Gamma_R^{\rm pro}(N_UE)\circ i_!^{\rm pro}(d_r(E))\circ e_i(Rr_*^{\rm et}E).$$
Both squares are natural in $E$. No flatness of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), its cartesian open-adjunction normalization; Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings). Agent-stated coefficient/site naturality of these specified maps, not an additional assertion quoted verbatim from either tag.

proof.text: On the etale sites, write $\lambda_v:T_Vv_{*,A}^{-1}\to v_{*,B}^{-1}T_W$ for the canonical tensor/pullback comparison supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The maps $q_p$ and $q_r$ are, by their definitions, the adjoint transposes of the corresponding $A$-counits after applying $T$. For the cartesian square, [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] identifies $\Gamma_R^{\rm et}$ as the open-adjunction adjunct of the inverse of the proper/open exchange. Apply the mate-pasting identities of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the rectangle formed by the two proper adjunctions, the two open adjunctions, and $T$. The two composites in the displayed etale equality are the mates of the same composite on inverse images: the tensor comparisons only reassociate $T$ with the inverse-image functors, while the proper and open factors are respectively the counit mates and the open-extension comparisons. Uniqueness of mates gives exactly the displayed equality, with no flatness assumption on $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Existence, uniqueness, naturality; the coefficient comparison is the adjoint transpose, and the proper/open map is normalized by its open adjunct

proof.text: For the site equation, use the exact comparison functor $N=\nu^*$ and its inverse-image compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For a proper edge $v$, the map $d_v$ is the specified counit mate and satisfies the counit normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. For an open edge $a$, $e_a$ is the natural extension-by-zero comparison, compatible with composition, by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Transport the same mate rectangle from Step 1 across $N$: the tensor comparison is natural by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], the proper and open sides become $d_v$ and $e_a$, and the transported open-adjunction prescription is precisely the definition of $\Gamma_R^{\rm pro}$. The mate-pasting identities therefore identify both sides with the same transported mate, yielding the displayed pro-etale equality on every bounded-below etale-origin object.

source.place: Existence, uniqueness, naturality; transport of the adjoint-transpose comparison through the site comparison

proof.text: Every constituent map in both composites is natural in the input: this is part of the naturality assertions for the tensor comparison, the proper/open interchange, the direct-image counit mate, and the extension-by-zero comparison cited above. Composition of natural transformations is natural, so both displayed equalities are natural in $E$.
